article.headline: Exelixis, A Cancer Drug Maker, Trades Near High Ahead Of Oct. 29 Report
article.deck: Exelixis is 4.8% past the 59.82 buy point of a five-week flat base, at the top of a buy range that ends at 62.81, with its RS line at a new high.
body: Exelixis makes cancer drugs. Its main franchise is cabozantinib, a pill that blocks several tyrosine kinases involved in tumor growth, sold as Cabometyx for advanced kidney cancer and as Cometriq for a form of thyroid cancer. The company also sells Cotellic and works on new oncology medicines for hard-to-treat cancers, mainly in the U.S.

The business keeps growing. June-quarter EPS rose 26.2% to 82 cents on revenue up 10.6% to $628.7 million. Revenue rose in each of the four quarters given, from $597.8 million to $598.7 million to $610.8 million to $628.7 million. EPS has been less even, running 69 cents, 88 cents, 79 cents and 82 cents. The company said it will report third-quarter results Thursday, Oct. 29.

The market does not pay much for that record. Exelixis carries a market value of about $15.5 billion and trades at 14.7 times forward earnings and 19.8 times trailing earnings. A recent headline asked whether the stock is fully valued as its cabozantinib patent window comes into focus, which is the question hanging over the multiple.

The chart is in better shape than the valuation would suggest. Exelixis rose 0.45, or 0.7%, to 62.68 Monday on volume 0.85x its 50-day average. It broke out Oct. 9 from a five-week flat base that ran 8.7% deep from its Sept. 3 high to its Sept. 11 low, on volume 1.12x average. The buy point is 59.82, and at 4.8% above it the stock sits just under the 62.81 top of the buy range.

The trend underneath is firm. The stock trades 10.0% above its 50-day line at 56.96 and 1.24 ATRs above its 21-day line at 59.58, not stretched. It is 1.1% under its 52-week high of 63.39 and has nearly doubled off its 52-week low of 33.76. Its RS line hit a new high, and it holds an RS rank of 88 of 99 on the desk's list. Shares are up 43.0% year to date and 59.9% over a year.
Recent headlines said Exelixis is poised to beat earnings estimates again and that cancer drug spending is headed past $400 billion.

With six sessions since the breakout and the stock at the top of its range, the next decision point is the Oct. 29 report. A move past 62.81 would take the stock out of the buy range; a pullback toward the 21-day line would keep the base intact.
article.watch: The Oct. 29 third-quarter report and the 62.81 top of the buy range.

body: Fortinet rose 2.37, or 1.4%, to 171.50 Monday, finding support at its 50-day moving average. article.headline: Pfizer Slips As Dividend Freeze Draws Cash Flow Questions
article.deck: Pfizer sits just 0.4% above the 29.31 buy point of a six-week flat base, in range to 30.78, with weak earnings underneath.
body: Pfizer fell 0.14, or 0.5%, to 29.44 Monday on volume 0.62x its 50-day average. The stock broke out Oct. 15 from a six-week flat base, 7.2% deep from its Sept. 3 high to its Oct. 5 low. The buy point is 29.31 and the buy range runs to 30.78; the close sits 0.4% above the buy point. The breakout session traded at 0.97x average.

Two sessions after the breakout, Pfizer is 1.5% under its 52-week high of 29.88. It trades 5.1% above its 50-day line at 28.02 and 1.41 ATRs above its 21-day line at 28.48. The RS rank is 75 of 99 on the desk's list; the RS line is 12.6% below its high. The stock is up 18.2% year to date.

The earnings do not match the chart. Pfizer lost 4 cents a share in the June quarter, a 107.8% decline from a year earlier, on revenue up 2.6% to $15.03 billion. EPS over the four quarters given swung from 62 cents to a 29-cent loss, to 47 cents, to the 4-cent loss. The next report is due Nov. 3. The stock trades at 10.2 times forward earnings, with a market value near $167.8 billion.
A 24/7 Wall St. headline Monday said Pfizer's dividend freeze raises a bigger question about its cash flow.
The close sits barely above the buy point. A close back under 29.31 would stall the breakout.
article.watch: The 29.31 buy point, which the stock has little room above, and the Nov. 3 report.

market_note: The Nasdaq rose 1.1% to 26,430.89 and the S&P 500 added 0.4% to 7,690.73, while the Dow slipped 0.1% to 51,966.03. All three closed below their 50-day lines: the S&P 500 by 0.2%, the Nasdaq by 0.7% and the Dow by 0.9%. The S&P 500 carries 6 distribution days over the last 25 sessions, the Dow 5 and the Nasdaq 3, and the desk's label stays at Market in correction. Leadership on the desk's list is narrow and oily: six names hold breakouts from the past week, four of them oil producers (ConocoPhillips, ExxonMobil, Chevron, EOG Resources) plus Visa and Pfizer, with energy third among groups on average RS behind AI chips and software. After hours, Cameco jumped 7.9% to 87.12 and Merck rose 3.4% to 148.57, while SLB fell 7.3% to 45.52, Steel Dynamics 5.1% to 232.64 and Alcoa 3.7% to 40.13.
